chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The boundary of Arafat is from the two Mazamin up to the furthest point of the Standing Station.

key_terms.الْمَأْزِمَيْنِ: The two Mazamin, specific landmarks marking the start of Arafat's boundary
key_terms.الْمَوْقِفِ: The Standing Station (Wuquf), referring to the ritual standing at Arafat
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the plain where pilgrims stand during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What are the defined boundaries of Arafat for Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the precise geographical limits of the plain of Arafat, establishing the validity of the essential Hajj station (wuquf) between the two Mazamin and the furthest extent of the standing area. In Shia jurisprudence, this definition is critical for determining the validity of pilgrimage, as the entire plain is considered a single valid place for standing, accommodating the diverse practices of the faithful. The narration underscores the importance of adhering to these divinely sanctioned boundaries to ensure the ritual's completeness.
